heartbeat.title: Watchdog ping
heartbeat.sub: A sign of life sent to your own watchdog (Uptime Kuma push, Healthchecks): if this server fails completely, the watchdog notices. That holds even when the machine, container or power is gone and nothing here can send a message any more. In a critical state the ping reports “down”.
heartbeat.off: Off – without a watchdog address nothing leaves the server.

flavor.silent: sign of life only (nothing when critical)

state.held: reported good – critical only after 2 min

heartbeat.error: Last ping failed ({count}× in a row): {error}
heartbeat.sent_none: State critical – nothing sent (type: sign of life only)
heartbeat.privacy: Privacy: only a GET request without content is sent. A watchdog on the internet sees your public IP address (roughly locatable) and how often the ping arrives – ideally run it in your own network.
heartbeat.where: Configure under System → Settings → Dashboard & access (“Watchdog ping”).

clock.red_title: Red light: keeps your eyes adapted to the dark (observatory, bedroom, server room at night)
clock.full_title: Full screen on or off (key F)
clock.tone_line: For setting clocks without radio or network: a beep on every full second, a long tone on the minute.
clock.tone_running: Running · expected accuracy {acc} (goal ± 5 ms), speaker delay not included.
clock.tone_unsynced: Running · not yet matched with the server – the beeps follow this device's clock for now.
clock.tone_blocked: The browser is still holding the sound – tap “Second beeps” or “Set a clock” once more.
clock.tone_unsupported: Your browser cannot play sound here.
clock.tone_info: The sound only starts after your click (browsers play nothing otherwise). “Second beeps”: a short beep on every full second of server time, a long tone on the full minute. “Set a clock”: a countdown of the last 10 seconds before the full minute, the long tone is 0 – that is when you press the button on the oven, in the car or on your watch. Beeps are scheduled with the browser's audio clock and the measured offset to the server; the expected accuracy is the match (± half the round trip) plus the audio clock's step, goal ± 5 ms. Not included is the delay inside the speaker: Bluetooth headphones and speakers lag 100 to 300 ms, built-in speakers hardly at all.
clock.device_line_unknown: Almost done: the page compares this device's clock with the time server.
clock.device_line_good: Fine – less than 0.1 s off, measured to within {acc}.
clock.device_line_warn: Noticeably off, fine for everyday use: phones usually take the time from the mobile network, PCs from the internet.
clock.device_line_crit: Clearly off: turn on “Set time automatically” in your device settings.
clock.device_line_uncertain: Measured only to within {acc} – not enough to tell for sure whether your device is less than 0.1 s off. Try again on a faster network.
clock.device_info: Like NTP, the page uses four timestamps to measure how far this device's clock is off the server clock (± half the round trip). The result stays in this browser: it is neither stored nor sent to the server or anywhere else. Traffic light: green below 0.1 s (including the measurement accuracy), yellow below 1 s, red from 1 s; grey when the measurement is too imprecise to tell. Phones usually set their clock from the mobile network or NTP, computers from a time server on the internet – depending on the device and the last sync they are milliseconds to seconds off. Some browsers round their clock on purpose (fingerprinting protection, e.g. to 1 ms or 100 ms); small values are less precise then.
clock.egg_possible: 23:59:60 would be possible today: on 30 June and 31 December the last minute (UTC) may get a leap second – none is announced this time.
clock.egg_insert: There is a leap second tonight: 23:59:59 UTC is followed by 23:59:60.
clock.egg_delete: One second is dropped today: 23:59:58 UTC is followed directly by the new day (negative leap second).
clock.stale_detail: the clock keeps running with the last match
clock.sync_jump: uncertain · device clock jumped or standby, waiting for a new sync
clock.band_title: Server: accuracy of the server clock according to chrony. Match: measurement of this page against the server (± half the round trip of the best of five measurements). The error bound of the display (line below the clock) also includes the server, drift and screen refresh.
clock.wake_https: Screen lock: can only be disabled over HTTPS

keys.u: UTC large or local time large
keys.t: tenths for stopwatch and timer; in the timecode design tenths or frames

clock.keys_note: With lock=1 in the address the shortcuts are off. Esc closes.
clock.hint_no_timer: The target comes from the address (until) and runs the same on every screen – it cannot be paused.
clock.tc_info: This line shows the server's time of day in timecode format. It is a display, not a reference signal: there is no house reference (black burst, tri-level), so no genlock. Your monitor draws at its own rate – a 60 Hz monitor cannot show 25 or 50 frames per second evenly. Browsers round their timers, with fingerprinting protection (e.g. Firefox with resistFingerprinting) to as much as 100 ms; the clock detects this, greys out the fine digit and names the reason. Expect a deviation of ± 1 to 2 frames. The fine digit shows tenths; frames are shown only on explicit request (sub=frames or key T). It turns grey when the error bound exceeds half a frame (50 ms for tenths) and disappears when the display counts as uncertain. At 29.97 and 59.94 fps the clock counts drop-frame (separator “;”). Real timecode comes from LTC or VITC generators.
clock.tc_unsure_tenths: tenths uncertain: display {acc}, reliable up to {limit}
clock.tc_unsure_frames: frames uncertain: display {acc}, half a frame is {limit}
clock.tc_grain: fine digit uncertain: your browser rounds its timers to {grain}
clock.tc_grain_unknown: fine digit uncertain: your browser rounds its timers very coarsely
clock.tc_reduced: frames off because your system asks for reduced motion
clock.hint_tc_reduced: Frames are not available while your system asks for reduced motion – tenths remain.
clock.hint_tc_noseconds: Without seconds there is no fine digit.
clock.world_more_one: {count} more time zone does not fit here
clock.world_more_other: {count} more time zones do not fit here
clock.custom_line: Applies on this device when you open /clock without parameters. Empty fields use the default. Kiosk, lock and the tile layout belong in the link (dashboard, “Displays” tab) so you can always get back here.
clock.custom_url_note: This address brings its own values. Apply opens /clock without them.
clock.custom_copy_failed: Copying is not possible. The link: {link}
clock.ptp_title: State of PTP on the server (ptp4l). More on the dashboard.
clock.holdover_title: Holdover: the server clock has no reference right now and keeps running on the frequency it learned last. Accuracy degrades over time.
clock.test_warn: Warning: the area switches between light and dark every second. Do not put it on air or show it to an audience. Esc ends it.
clock.test_note: The area switches exactly on the full second, the click falls on the same second. If you see the switch after the click, raise the lead (arrow keys) until both coincide. Bluetooth speakers delay the click – measure with a cable or the built-in speaker.
clock.test_note_locked: The area switches exactly on the full second, the click falls on the same second. The controls are locked (lock=1): you cannot set the lead here. Change lead= in the link or open the test pattern without lock=1. Bluetooth speakers delay the click – measure with a cable or the built-in speaker.
clock.test_lead: Lead {ms} ms · in the link: lead={ms}
clock.test_tone_on: Click runs on every full second.
clock.test_tone_blocked: The browser is still holding the sound – tap “Click sound” once more.
clock.test_reduced: The test pattern does not start: your system asks for reduced motion, so there is no flashing area here. Turn the setting off in your operating system if you want to calibrate the lead.
clock.test_eink: There is no test pattern on e-ink: the display only changes once a minute.
clock.test_ended_stored: Test pattern ended · lead {ms} ms remembered
clock.hint_signal_on: On Air on – this device only
clock.hint_signal_off: On Air off on this device
clock.hint_signal_central: Central signal is on – the O key has no effect right now
clock.timer_line: Runs in this browser only. Start, pause and reset also with the space bar and R.
clock.timer_info: The time runs in this browser only and is neither stored nor sent anywhere; reloading the page clears it. It uses the browser's monotonic clock, so changing the device clock does not disturb it. The sound only beeps while the page is open and the device is awake – it is no alarm clock. If the page is in a background tab, the clock schedules the sounds ahead when you switch away; if the browser discards the tab or the device sleeps, there is still no sound. Browsers only play sound after a click, so switch on “Sound at the end” yourself. Pomodoro: work and break alternate on their own, every fourth break is long (three times as long, at most 30 min, but never shorter than the normal break). Durations via the address: ?pomo=50m&pause=10m.
clock.timer_blocked: This clock counts to a fixed target from the address or profile. For the egg timer and Pomodoro open /clock without a target.
clock.egg_bad: I don't understand this duration – minutes (7), minutes:seconds (7:30) or 1h30m, at most 24 h.
clock.pomo_say_long: Pomodoro done, take a long break.
clock.timer_tone_on: Sound on: three short beeps before the end, a long one at the end.
clock.timer_tone_blocked: The browser does not allow sound yet – tap the page once.
clock.own_line: Up to five, remembered in this browser only. For many screens put the target in the link or a profile (dashboard, tab “Displays”).
clock.own_unsaved: Remembered only until reload: this browser does not allow storing. Use the link or a profile.
clock.own_bad: Target like 20:15 or 2026-12-31T23:59, label with 1 to 24 characters.

clock.moon_click_south: Click: show it as seen from the southern hemisphere.
clock.moon_click_north: Click: show it as seen from the northern hemisphere.
clock.hint_moon_south: Moon as seen from the southern hemisphere
clock.hint_moon_north: Moon as seen from the northern hemisphere
clock.moon_info: Calculated right here in the browser, without a location and without fetching anything. The phase is the same everywhere on Earth; new and full moon are correct to about ±1 day (usually much better). In the southern hemisphere the picture is mirrored – click the moon to flip it. Only this browser remembers that.
clock.game_line: Tap “Now!” exactly when the clock reaches the full second or minute.
clock.game_wait: Not matched with the server yet – starting in a moment.
clock.game_within: That is within the measuring accuracy.
clock.game_detail: Measuring accuracy: match {device} (half round trip) · server {server} · frame {frame}
clock.game_unsaved: New best – the browser does not allow storing it, it only lasts until you reload.
clock.game_note: The best value stays in this browser only.
clock.game_info: The moment of your tap (mouse, finger or key) is taken from the browser's monotonic clock and converted to this clock's server time – the same time shown in large digits. The deviation counts to the nearest full second or minute: negative early, positive late. The game cannot be more exact than the measurement: match with the server (half the round trip), accuracy of the server clock and one frame until the new digit is visible. Touch screens and wireless mice add their own delay. The best value is kept in this browser's storage only, nothing is sent.
clock.tone_pips_line: Time signal like on the radio: five short pips, the long one is the full hour or minute. Just for fun, not a reference: browser and speakers delay the sound by a few to well over 100 ms.
clock.tone_pips_running: Time signal running ({scope}). Browser audio and speakers delay the sound – not a reference.
clock.egg_dst_forward: Today the clock goes forward by {min} minutes – less sleep.
clock.egg_dst_back: Today the clock goes back by {min} minutes – time for free.
clock.egg_konami: ↑ ↑ ↓ ↓ ← → ← → B A – binary clock unlocked until you reload.
